Donaldson qualifies for an automatic 50% remission of his sentence as the offences were committed before a change in the law that gave judges discretion over what portion is spent in custody, meaning he will spend 7-1/2 years in prison, the Lady Chief Justice's Office of Northern Ireland said. Donaldson immediately stepped down as head of the Democratic Unionist Party, founded by Protestant cleric Ian Paisley at the height of three decades of sectarian bloodshed, which ended after a 1998 peace deal. He was knighted by the late Queen Elizabeth for his political services in 2016 and was central to the negotiation of a key post-Brexit trade deal just two months prior to his arrest. He asked for his knighthood [USN:L8N42W1PI TEXT:"to be renounced"] two days after his conviction. The jury also found that Donaldson's wife, Eleanor, aided and abetted her husband. She has also denied the charges. The court ruled her unfit to stand trial last month, due to mental health issues, meaning she could not face criminal conviction.

item.title: Ataque de drones contra dos petroleros deja siete desaparecidos frente a costa rumana
item.description: Equipos de rescate buscaban el jueves a siete marinos desaparecidos después de que unos drones atacaron dos buques cisterna para productos químicos cerca de la costa rumana del mar Negro, provocando un incendio y suscitando preocupaciones de seguridad en una ruta vital para Ucrania.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Equipos de rescate buscaban el jueves a siete marinos desaparecidos después de que unos drones atacaron dos buques cisterna para productos químicos cerca de la costa rumana del mar Negro, provocando un incendio y suscitando preocupaciones de seguridad en una ruta vital para Ucrania. El presidente rumano, Nicusor Dan, afirmó que los dos buques fueron alcanzados por drones, pero se negó a precisar si Rusia era la responsable. "Dos drones aéreos los alcanzaron", declaró Dan a la prensa en Bruselas antes de una cumbre de líderes de la Unión Europea, y añadió que Rumanía seguía recabando información apenas unas horas después de los ataques. "Habrá una reacción por parte del Estado rumano". Los buques estaban fondeados cerca de la desembocadura del canal de Sulina, que conduce al río Danubio, una importante ruta de exportación usada por Ucrania ante los repetidos ataques rusos contra sus puertos del mar Negro. Uno estaba en aguas territoriales rumanas y el otro, justo fuera. Los tripulantes desaparecidos formaban parte de los 12 marinos a bordo del petrolero Wine Trader, con bandera de San Marino, que fue alcanzado a 13 millas náuticas al sureste del canal, cerca de aguas rumanas. Cinco tripulantes fueron rescatados, según las autoridades rumanas. El segundo buque, el petrolero y químico Yara J, con bandera de Comoras, se incendió tras ser alcanzado a entre 8 y 10 millas al sureste de Sulina, dentro de aguas rumanas, a última hora del miércoles. Todos sus tripulantes estaban a salvo. Estos ataques son los últimos de una serie de ataques contra la navegación mercante en la parte occidental del mar Negro. Al menos otros cinco buques de carga han sido atacados cerca de las costas de Rumanía y de la vecina Bulgaria, miembros de la OTAN, en los últimos diez días, con al menos 23 marineros desaparecidos o fallecidos. Los incidentes ocurrieron fuera de las aguas territoriales de la alianza. El Ministerio del Interior informó de que envió dos helicópteros Black Hawk para la misión de búsqueda y rescate, así como dos buques con personal médico a bordo. "En este momento, el rescate no puede realizarse de forma segura debido al fuerte oleaje", señaló en un comunicado. La OTAN dijo en un comunicado que está en contacto con las autoridades rumanas. NUEVOS ATAQUES Añadió que otros dos buques fueron atacados en el mar Negro: el granelero Sea Destiny, con pabellón de Islas Marshall, que estaba en aguas rumanas, y el petrolero Dania J, con bandera de Tanzania, amarrado en el puerto ucraniano de Izmail, en el Danubio. No se mencionaron víctimas. "La OTAN seguirá colaborando de forma estrecha con nuestros aliados en el mar Negro, ajustando nuestra postura de disuasión y defensa según sea necesario", indicó el secretario general de la OTAN, Mark Rutte, tras reunirse con Dan y el primer ministro búlgaro, Rumen Radev. Rumanía comparte una frontera de 614 kilómetros con Ucrania, gran parte de ella a lo largo del Danubio. Ha denunciado reiteradas incursiones de drones rusos en su espacio aéreo desde el inicio de la invasión de Ucrania por parte de Moscú en 2022. La escalada de ataques contra la navegación en el mar Negro ha agravado la preocupación por las exportaciones de cereales de la región. Los ataques rusos contra los puertos ucranianos del mar Negro han obligado a Kiev a depender más del Danubio y las rutas marítimas cercanas a las costas de Rumanía y Bulgaria. Ucrania, por su parte, ha atacado buques rusos cerca de la desembocadura del río Don, en el mar de Azov. Radev afirmó que los líderes de la UE debatirán una propuesta de moratoria sobre los ataques a buques civiles en el mar Negro. "Consideramos el mar Negro una arteria del suministro mundial de alimentos", dijo la ministra rumana de Relaciones Exteriores, Oana Toiu, en una conferencia de seguridad celebrada en Varsovia esta semana. "Actualmente es, por desgracia, el mar más mortífero si se tiene en cuenta el número de víctimas entre los marineros en los últimos meses. Eso significa que tenemos que aumentar nuestras inversiones en disuasión y defensa", agregó.

item.title: El oro repunta por la debilidad del dólar y la caída de los rendimientos en EEUU
item.description: El oro subió más de un 1% el jueves, para romper una racha de tres sesiones de pérdidas, respaldado por la debilidad del dólar y el descenso de los rendimientos de los bonos del Tesoro de Estados Unidos, mientras que las expectativas de que la Reserva Federal suba las tasas este mes eran moderadas a pesar de que los datos de inflación fueron más altos de lo esperado.
item.dc:creator: Pablo Sinha
item.content:encoded: El oro subió más de un 1% el jueves, para romper una racha de tres sesiones de pérdidas, respaldado por la debilidad del dólar y el descenso de los rendimientos de los bonos del Tesoro de Estados Unidos, mientras que las expectativas de que la Reserva Federal suba las tasas este mes eran moderadas a pesar de que los datos de inflación fueron más altos de lo esperado. El oro al contado ganó un 1,1%, a 4.149 dólares por onza, a las 1636 GMT, tras caer a un mínimo de una semana en la sesión anterior. Los futuros del oro estadounidense para entrega en diciembre avanzaron un 1,5%, a 4.170,10 dólares por onza. El dólar (.DXY) caía un 0,4%, mientras que el rendimiento de referencia de los bonos del Tesoro a 10 años se situaba en un mínimo de tres semanas. "Creo que el mercado ya anticipaba en gran medida los altos datos del índice de precios al productor (IPP), tras las cifras del índice de precios al consumidor (IPC) de ayer (miércoles), que superaron las expectativas", dijo Peter Grant, vicepresidente y estratega sénior de metales en Zaner Metals. "El mercado está empezando a darse cuenta de que la Fed tiene las manos atadas en cierta medida debido a la situación fiscal y de que subir las tasas de interés mucho más supondrá una carga considerable para la economía". Unas tasas de interés más altas hacen que los activos que no generan rendimiento resulten menos atractivos. Los precios al productor de Estados Unidos anotaron en septiembre su mayor subida en cuatro años y medio, en un contexto de aumento de los costos de los bienes y servicios, lo que constituye el más reciente indicio de que la inflación se está traspasando de la energía a otros productos. Los datos se sumaron al informe sobre los precios al consumidor publicado el miércoles, que mostró una aceleración de los precios en septiembre debido al aumento de los costos de la gasolina. Sin embargo, la presidenta de la Fed de San Francisco, Mary Daly, y la vicepresidenta de Supervisión, Michelle Bowman, subrayaron que quizá no sea necesaria una subida inmediata de las tasas, lo que moderó las expectativas de un alza en octubre. Entre otros metales, la plata al contado trepó un 2,3%, a 56,90 dólares por onza; el platino subió un 0,4%, a 1.613,75 dólares; y el paladio sumó un 3,2%, a 1.129,20 dólares la onza.

item.title: TSX rises as lower bond yields offset tech, energy weakness
item.description: Canada's main stock index rose on Thursday, as lower bond yields boosted risk appetite, offsetting weakness in energy shares caused by falling oil prices and a global selloff in AI-related technology stocks.
item.dc:creator: Utkarsh Hathi
item.content:encoded: Canada's main stock index rose on Thursday, as lower bond yields boosted risk appetite, offsetting weakness in energy shares caused by falling oil prices and a [USN:L1N4610FG TEXT:"global selloff "]in AI-related technology stocks. The S&P/TSX Composite Index (.GSPTSE) was up 0.52% at 35,770 points by 10:41 a.m. ET, rebounding after sharp declines in the previous session. Canada's benchmark 10-year bond yield slipped about 8 basis points to 3.795%, driving broad sectoral gains Materials sector (.GSPTTMT) , including metal miners, gained 1.4% as precious metal prices rebounded on a softer dollar Chip stocks globally extended losses as concerns about increased borrowing costs unsettled investors, dragging Wall Street's Nasdaq down 0.7% Canadian tech equities (.SPTTTK) declined 0.7%, with e-commerce platform Shopify (SHOP.TO) slipping 1.4% and electronics equipment firm Celestica (CLS.TO) down 7.7% "The sector has continued to be under pressure that started at the beginning of the year, except (for) the relief rally in the spring and summer," said Shiraz Ahmed, CEO of Sartorial Wealth "The moat around their (software) business is not quite as strong, now that AI and the ability to effectively recreate software has become very commoditized" Energy sector (.SPTTEN) slipped 0.5% as oil prices eased 0.7% after a US official on Wednesday signaled potential US steps to ease restriction on Russia's "shadow fleet" tankers Canadian [USN:AQN2MO654 TEXT:"factory sales"] grew 1.5% in August from July on higher sales of primary metals, data showed on Thursday Still, economists remain cautious about recovery in manufacturing considering limited sectoral gains "This reinforces our view that the Bank of Canada will deliver only two of the roughly four rate hikes currently priced in by markets, with tightening serving more as a risk-management exercise against upside inflation risks," said Thomas Ryan, senior North America economist, Capital Economics

item.title: Trump donor leading Caucasus fund has major Armenia holdings, Russia business history
item.description: US President Donald Trump’s pick to lead a $201 million investment fund in the Caucasus holds major telecom and mining interests there and formerly ran a Russia-focused investment firm that touted close ties to the Kremlin, documents reviewed by Reuters show.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Landay, Alexandra Ulmer, Maria Tsvetkova
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump’s pick to lead a $201 million investment fund in the Caucasus holds major telecom and mining interests there and formerly ran a Russia-focused investment firm that touted close ties to the Kremlin, documents reviewed by Reuters show. Konstantin Sokolov, a 51-year-old Russian-born businessman, was put in charge of the investment vehicle, now called the Trans-Caspian Enterprise Fund, in January, according to its incorporation documents. He holds major stakes in Armenia’s top mobile phone company Viva Armenia, and purchased Armenia’s second largest copper and molybdenum mine earlier this year after receiving a special permit from the US government to buy it, according to the Reuters reporting. A Reuters review of public documents related to the only three other US enterprise funds now operating showed no indications that any of their heads have major investments in the countries where those funds invest. Bo Cutter, chairman of a US enterprise fund focused on Tunisia told Reuters he had "no business interests of any kind in Tunisia," without elaborating on whether and why that might pose a problem. Cutter declined to comment on Sokolov or the Trans-Caspian fund. Still, according to six ethics experts who reviewed the Reuters reporting, Sokolov’s business interests create a conflict of interest because his role gives him control of government money that could potentially benefit his companies. Ann Skeet, an ethics expert at Santa Clara University, said, "I think Congress should be asking questions." Reuters found no indication of any wrongdoing by Sokolov. US legislation governing such investment funds does not forbid directors from holding investments in regions of operation. A representative for Sokolov’s private equity firm, IJS Investments, said the fund was prohibited from investing in any of his businesses and that Sokolov had complied with "all due diligence and security requirements." A State Department spokesperson said the enterprise fund would comply with annual reporting requirements and independent audits "as well as with applicable grant provisions including conflict of interest requirements." Sokolov had been among a list of 37 corporate and individual donors to Trump’s White House ballroom project distributed by the White House last year. The Washington Post reported on Thursday that Sokolov donated $1 million to the project. Sokolov has also donated some $13 million to Republican political groups, according to Federal Election Commission data. ASCENDANT IN ARMENIA The Trans-Caspian fund is part of a broader US push to develop trade routes and investment across the South Caucasus and Central Asia, an effort that could reduce the region's reliance on Russian and Chinese infrastructure. The Trans-Caspian fund’s board, led by Sokolov, has the power to make grants, loans and investments across Armenia, Azerbaijan, Georgia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan. Its website lists critical minerals, energy and rail infrastructure among its top investment priorities. Sokolov has built up his business presence in Armenia rapidly in recent years. He and a Chinese business partner, Zhe Zhang, acquired control of Viva Armenia in January 2024 from Russia's largest mobile provider, MTS, according to company statements and Armenian corporate records. Zhang, a former Chinese Commerce Ministry diplomat, did not respond to requests for comment. Viva Armenia did not comment. More recently, Sokolov’s Texas-based Dynamic Frontier Holdings company said it was granted legal authorization from the US Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control on June 1 to buy Armenia’s Teghout mine from a sanctioned state-owned Russian bank, VTB. OFAC licenses authorize transactions that would otherwise be prohibited by US sanctions and typically take several months or years to process. Sokolov and a representative for the Teghout mine did not respond to questions about when they first applied for a license. A representative for Teghout said licenses and approvals for the transaction were obtained through OFAC’s "standard independent regulatory process." The US Treasury Department and VTB did not respond to requests for comment. None of the heads of the only other active US enterprise funds - which focus on Egypt, Tunisia, and Ukraine-Moldova - appear to have significant business interests in those countries, according to a Reuters review of public documents and their official biographies. James Harmon is chairman of the Egyptian fund, and Dennis Johnson is chairman of the Ukraine-Moldova fund. They did not respond to requests for comment. BACKGROUND IN RUSSIA Sokolov’s biography on his personal website highlights his modest upbringing in St. Petersburg and his dislike of the Soviet government, which he said sent his grandmother to a gulag. It says he immigrated to the United States at 21, several years after the collapse of the Soviet Union. But his ties to Russia went on long after he left, according to a Reuters review of corporate and government records. The businessman’s purported ties to the Russian government warrant scrutiny to ensure US interests come first in the fund’s management, said two of the ethics experts Reuters interviewed. "I'd want a very thorough security clearance review if I were in the US government," said Richard Painter, a University of Minnesota professor who served as ethics counsel to former Republican President George W. Bush. A 2015 promotional brochure reviewed by Reuters for the now-defunct Liechtenstein-registered Gotthard Investment Fund, a Russia-focused real estate investment operation, listed Sokolov as a fund manager and emphasized the fund’s "strong and long-lasting personal and professional trust relationships forged over the last 20 years with Moscow, St. Petersburg and Federal governments." A former project manager with the fund, speaking to Reuters on condition of anonymity, said they recognized the brochure as authentic. Lawyers representing Sokolov said that Sokolov "does not believe" the brochure is authentic, and that the logo on the brochure did not appear to be one used by the fund. "Mr. Sokolov has no relationships with Russian government officials or the Russian government," his representative told Reuters, adding "he does not hold a Russian citizenship." Reuters could not independently confirm Sokolov no longer has Russian citizenship. Sokolov used a Russian passport for international travel as late as 2016, according to travel records reviewed by Reuters. The White House referred requests for comment about Sokolov to the State Department. The State Department did not provide details on Sokolov’s background check or whether he had a security clearance. When asked for comment about Sokolov, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said: "We don’t know who you are talking about."

item.content:encoded: London's blue-chip stocks closed at a seven-week high on Thursday after the finance minister [USN:S8N4040BJ TEXT:"reaffirmed"] the government's commitment to fiscal discipline, while a shift into defensive sectors amid a deepening global selloff in AI-related stocks also supported the benchmark. item.title: Wall St banks caught in capital markets lull after a strong first half of 2026
item.description: Quarterly results from Wall Street's big banks this week showed that even the largest and most robust players of the industry can be vulnerable to the ebb and flow of capital markets.
item.dc:creator: Manya Saini
item.content:encoded: Quarterly results from Wall Street's big banks [USN:L1N45Z0O3 TEXT:"this week showed"] that even the largest and most robust players of the industry can be vulnerable to the ebb and flow of capital markets. Dealmaking, a cyclical business, slowed in the third quarter and dented investment banking, as rising bond yields, choppy AI trade and geopolitical worries gave jitters to investors and corporate boardrooms alike, [USN:L6N45M0VD TEXT:"further delaying"] a long-awaited revival in M&As and IPOs. Here is an overview of results from the six top US banks in charts, which kicked off the third-quarter earnings season for US companies: TWO MISSES, LITTLE MARKET CHEER JPMorgan Chase (JPM.N) posted its [USN:L4N45Z10B TEXT:"first profit miss"] since the fourth quarter of 2023, according to LSEG data, while its closest rival, Bank of America (BAC.N) , [USN:L4N4600XY TEXT:"fell short"] of market expectations. The other four top US banks exceeded expectations, but their stocks traded lower or did not react as investors judged the earnings beats to be smaller than in previous quarters. DEALMAKING STALLS Dealmakers were looking forward to a bumper year, but momentum has stalled since the summer as market volatility, geopolitical turmoil, rising Treasury yields and concerns over the sustainability of the AI trade kept companies on the sidelines. Growth in investment banking fees slowed sharply compared to the prior quarter as an interest-rate hike and delays to several high-profile IPOs hit sentiment, even though executives reassured investors that they have not been canceled. EQUITY AND FIXED-INCOME DESKS DIVERGE The quarterly results revealed a sharp divide in trading performance at big banks: equity desks benefited from a surge in market activity, while fixed-income underperformed. Market volatility typically boosts trading businesses as clients reposition portfolios and hedge against risks. CONSUMER BANKING: A STEADY ENGINE Net interest income, the difference between what banks earn on loans and pay out on deposits, rose, with analysts expecting further support from the Federal Reserve's September rate hike. Banking executives [USN:L4N45V0N5 TEXT:"pointed to resilient consumer spending"] and borrowing, easing concerns that sticky inflation and elevated rates would strain household budgets. In a bright spot, loan demand also continued to chug along.
